name: awesome-tunneling
desc: List of ngrok, Cloudflare Tunnel, Tailscale, and ZeroTier alternatives and other tunneling software and services. Focus on self-hosting.

resources.name: Telebit
resources.desc: Written in JS. Code.

resources.name: tunnel.pyjam.as
resources.desc: No custom client; uses WireGuard directly instead. Written in Python. source code

resources.name: SSH-J.com
resources.desc: Public SSH Jump & Port Forwarding server. No software, no registration, just an anonymous SSH server for forwarding. Users are encouraged to use it for SSH exposure only, to preserve end-to-end encryption. No public ports, only in-SSH connectivity. Run ssh ssh-j.com and it will display usage information.

resources.name: Greenhouse
resources.desc: Instant least-authority port-forwarding with automatic HTTPS; the authors "really don't want your TLS private keys." The hosted service (greenhouse.server.garden) is currently unavailable and the project appears unmaintained (last activity 2023).

resources.name: YTunnel
resources.desc: MIT Licensed, Rust powered, uses your domains and creates Cloudflare Tunnels with easy to use TUI ![ytunnel github stars badge](https://github.com/yetidevworks/ytunnel)

resources.name: wireport
resources.desc: Multi-protocol tunneling (HTTP[S]/2, WebSockets, gRPC, TCP, UDP, auto-TLS/SSL). Securely resolves remote Docker container names as local hostnames. Easy self-hosting (no tinkering with docker-compose and configs). MIT License. Written in Go.

resources.name: ngrok 2.0
resources.desc: Probably the gold standard and most popular. Closed source. Lots of features, including TLS and TCP tunnels. Doesn't require root to run client.

resources.name: Webhook Relay
resources.desc: Hosted HTTP/TCP tunnels and webhook forwarding to private services through an outbound client. Provides stable hostnames, custom domains with automatic HTTPS, and a Kubernetes operator; an account and paid plan are required for bidirectional tunnels.

resources.name: Cloudflare Tunnel
resources.desc: Excellent free option. Nicely integrates tunneling with the rest of Cloudflare's products, which include DNS and auto HTTPS. Client source code is Apache 2.0 licensed and written in Golang.

resources.name: Microsoft Dev Tunnels
resources.desc: Not as useful for self-hosting (no custom domains and it shows warnings when people visit the URLs), but a solid option for dev work.

resources.name: Livecycle Docker Extension
resources.desc: Offer much more than just tunneling. Have a collaboration layer (Dashboard) that allows you to bring collaborations, debug, and gather feedback from the people you are working with. Share HTTPS URLs.

resources.name: Beeceptor
resources.desc: Goes beyond tunneling. Rest API mocking and intercepting tool. You can view the live requests and send mocked responses. Written in JavaScript.

resources.name: Pinggy
resources.desc: SSH based single command HTTPS / TCP / TLS tunnels, no downloads required. Rich terminal interface and a web debugger. Free tier - 60 min timeout. The paid tier allows custom domains with built-in Let's Encrypt certificates.

resources.name: tuns.sh
resources.desc: SSH-based hosted tunnel from pico.sh. Uses the system SSH client with no additional installation; ssh -R dev:80:localhost:3000 tuns.sh exposes a local service at https://{user}-dev.tuns.sh with automatic HTTPS. Supports HTTP/WSS/TCP tunnels, custom domains, US/EU regions, and per-site analytics. Requires pico+ ($2/month billed yearly); the backend is open-source sish.

resources.name: Loophole
resources.desc: Offers end-to-end TLS encryption with the client automatically getting certs from Let's Encrypt. QR codes for URL sharing. The client is open source. Can serve a local directory over WebDAV. MIT License. Written in Go.

resources.name: localhost.run
resources.desc: Simple hosted SSH option. Supports custom domains for a cost.

resources.name: Packetriot
resources.desc: Comprehensive alternative to ngrok. HTTP Inspector, Let's Encrypt integration, doesn't require root and Linux repos for apt, yum and dnf. Enterprise licenses and self-hosted option.

resources.name: Horizon Tunnel
resources.desc: Easy to use HTTP(S) and websocket tunneling aimed at development. Free tier available. Fixed URL is part of paid plans.

resources.name: Hoppy
resources.desc: WireGuard-based. Provides static IPv4 and IPv6 addresses for your machines, which is a simple and useful level of abstraction. Targeted towards self-hosters and people behind NATs.

resources.name: gw.run
resources.desc: Specifically focusing on securely exposing internal web apps to a group of people; not for publicly facing apps. Share access via email address then allow users to log in with common login providers like Google.

resources.name: SSHReach.me
resources.desc: Paid SSH-based option. Uses a simple Python script.

resources.name: KubeSail
resources.desc: Company offering tunneling, dynamic DNS, and other services for self-hosting with Kubernetes.

resources.name: inlets
resources.desc: Used to be open source; now focused on a polished commercial offering. Designed to work well with Kubernetes.

resources.name: LocalToNet
resources.desc: Supports UDP. Free for a single tunnel. Paid supports custom domains.

resources.name: LocalXpose
resources.desc: Looks like a solid paid option, with a limited free tier.

resources.name: Tabserve.dev
resources.desc: Web UI that runs entirely in the browser and uses a Cloudflare Worker for https.

resources.name: TunnelAPI 2.0
resources.desc: With a lot of features for teams and enterprises, including the AI API Gateway (a single gateway to multiple models), API Workflow, and exposing localhost to the internet with a custom subdomain. Doesn't require root to run the client.

resources.name: Serveo
resources.desc: SSH-based, signup optional, offering HTTP(S) and TCP tunneling and SSH jump host forwarding capabilities.

resources.name: Homeway
resources.desc: Secure and private remote access for Home Assistant. The free tier has a monthly data limit cap, but unlimited data is only $2.49/month.

resources.name: instatunnel
resources.desc: Hosted tunneling service offering HTTP/TCP tunnels and custom domain support. Suitable for quickly exposing local services with built-in HTTPS and simple setup. Allows for 3 simultaneous tunnels

resources.name: remote.it
resources.desc: Tunnels SSH, HTTP/S, TCP, Docker, popular database etc. allows mapping a local port to a remote port.

resources.name: LocalCan
resources.desc: Desktop app and CLI for Mac, Windows and Linux (CLI-only on Linux). HTTP and TCP tunnels with custom domains and automatic HTTPS, .local domains on the local network via mDNS, traffic inspection and replay, MCP server for AI agents. Free tier - one HTTP tunnel, 60 min sessions, 1 GB/month.

resources.name: Optimistix Tunnel
resources.desc: Easily expose your local server to the internet with simple SSH-based tunneling. Supports HTTP(S) and TCP. No signup, no install—just connect and go. Free plan available.

resources.name: GetPublicIP
resources.desc: Commercial service that routes a dedicated public IPv4/IPv6 address to a server behind NAT over WireGuard, with TCP, UDP, and ICMP support; users manage their own TLS.

resources.name: SteadIP
resources.desc: Offers both free and paid tunneling services. SteadIP Anchor gives your tunnel a dedicated IPv4 address, so your endpoint keeps a stable public IP instead of sharing one.

resources.name: ProxyLink
resources.desc: Exposes services behind NAT/CGNAT via HTTP/HTTPS/TCP/UDP links with automatic HTTPS, but the tunnel runs on the router or gateway rather than per-host: one WireGuard peer covers the whole LAN and any additional VLANs, so devices that can't run a client (NVRs, PBXs, managed switches) are reachable without installing anything on them. Also provides browser-based RDP, VNC and SSH sessions to those devices. Aimed at MSPs and IT teams rather than dev tunnels. Closed source, EU-hosted. Free during early access.

resources.name: Netrinos
resources.desc: Commercial WireGuard-based overlay VPN. Gateway mode reaches devices that can't run a client (IP cameras, NVRs, NAS, printers); 1:1 NAT lets sites with overlapping LAN subnets coexist; works behind CGNAT without port forwarding.

resources.name: Nebula
resources.desc: ![nebula github stars badge](https://github.com/slackhq/nebula/stargazers) Peer-to-peer overlay network. Developed and used internally by Slack. Similar to Tailscale but completely open source. Doesn't use WireGuard. Written in Go.

resources.name: Defined Networking
resources.desc: Commercial managed control plane for Nebula (above), from Nebula's original authors. Hosted certificate issuance/rotation, roles and firewall rules, SSO; the data plane is open source Nebula. Private overlay access rather than public-URL ingress.

resources.name: ZeroTier
resources.desc: ![zerotier github stars badge](https://github.com/zerotier/ZeroTierOne/stargazers) Layer 2 overlay network. They take decentralization seriously, and like to say "decentralize until it hurts, then centralize until it works." Written in C++.

resources.name: n2n
resources.desc: ![n2n github stars badge](https://github.com/ntop/n2n/stargazers) - Built on nodes and supernodes. GPL-3.0 license. Written in C.

resources.name: OpenZiti
resources.desc: ![OpenZiti github stars badge](https://github.com/openziti/ziti/stargazers) - Overlay network. The goal of OpenZiti is to extend zero trust all the way into your application, not just to your network. Apache 2.0 license. Written in Go.

resources.name: weron
resources.desc: ![weron github stars badge](https://github.com/pojntfx/weron/stargazers) - Built on WebRTC. Can create Layer 2 and Layer 3 networks. NAT traversal via STUN and TURN. AGPL-3.0 license. Written in Go.

resources.name: EdgeVPN
resources.desc: Fully decentralized, statically built P2P VPN on libp2p. No central server; peers discover each other via DHT. Supports file transfer and sharing TCP services between peers without a VPN interface. Apache 2.0 License. Written in Go.

resources.name: wsssh
resources.desc: Websocket jump host based SSH/SCP tunnelling with self hosted server.

resources.name: Nilloc
resources.desc: Developer-focused. Aims to have better pricing than ngrok. Free tier.

resources.name: Twingate
resources.desc: Commercial zero-trust network access service for private resources. Easy outbound connector model, but enrolled-user private access rather than public Internet ingress.

resources.name: Yggdrasil
resources.desc: ![yggdrasil github stars badge](https://github.com/yggdrasil-network/yggdrasil-go/stargazers) - An IPv6-only, end-to-end encrypted overlay network with routing between all network participants. LGPLv3 license. Written in Go.
